answer: An agent economy resists sybils with random-walk trust scoring: a few verified seed identities anchor the graph, and random walks spread trust along interaction edges, like water seeping through karst. The old fable of cheap fakes fails because fake clusters link mostly to each other, so walks from honest seeds rarely reach them and their scores stay near zero. The lagoon of rewards flows only to identities the walks visit, so an attacker must buy a genuine link into the honest region for every fake, paying full cost per fake while one honest agent earns from a single real connection.
